//months: activeMonths are California coastal timing (Salinas Valley, Santa Maria): spring and fall downy mildew pressure.
//enabled: Enabled: checks whose threshold is a published figure the sensor measures directly — air, leaf and soil temperature, humidity, durations, rates, pH. Disabled: checks whose threshold depends on this soil or this probe (volumetric moisture, EC, N, the 'wet' cut-off of a leaf-wetness sensor) or that need the forecast block — each says what to set before enabling it.

checks.//: ═══ FLEET HEALTH — every pack carries these, so the pack runs on its own. None needs crop tuning. ═══

═══ HEAT ═══ UC IPM: lettuce is stressed when temperatures stay above 24–27 °C (75–80 °F) — bolting, bitterness, tipburn (a calcium disorder made worse by heat and high fertility). Research reports early bolting above 30 °C. Sources: UC IPM, https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/cultural-tips-for-growing-lettuce/ ; UC IPM, "Tipburn", https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/GARDEN/VEGES/ENVIRON/lettipburn.html

DOWNY MILDEW (Bremia lactucae). UC IPM model (Scherm & van Bruggen; trials in Monterey and Santa Barbara counties, and UC describes it as "still in the validation stage"): "treat when the leaf wetness period ends at 10:00 a.m. or later (11:00 a.m. during Daylight Savings Time), after a minimum of a ten day spray interval". This check cannot see spray history, so it does not enforce the 10-day interval. UC places the sensor between plants, 10 cm above the soil. Later work (Wu et al. 2005) found higher midday temperature (10:00–14:00) lowers disease, a refinement not modelled here. activeHours [10] with activeHoursStandardTime runs the check in the 10:00 standard-time hour all year — 11:00 on the clock during daylight saving, switching exactly on the change dates — so a latest leaf.wetness reading above the cut-off means the leaves are still wet then. DISABLED: the 50 % wet cut-off is a placeholder — a leaf-wetness percentage means different things on different sensors; set max to this sensor's dry/wet boundary. Sources: UC IPM, lettuce downy mildew model, https://ipm.ucanr.edu/DISEASE/DATABASE/lettucedowny.html

ROOT-ZONE SALINITY — lettuce: Maas–Hoffman threshold ECe 1.3 dS/m, above which yield declines. DISABLED until converted to what the probe reads. Maas–Hoffman thresholds are saturated-paste ECe. A soil probe reports bulk EC (or pore EC), which is not ECe: FAO 29 gives soil-water EC ≈ 2 × ECe at field capacity, and bulk EC is lower than pore EC and moves with water content. Convert before enabling — take a saturated-paste lab sample beside the probe and scale this threshold by the probe/ECe ratio. Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29, ch. 2 and Annex 1 (Maas & Grattan 1999), https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e02.htm , https://www.fao.org/4/y4263e/y4263e0e.htm

SOIL pH — lettuce: outside 6.0–6.8. pH moves over seasons, not hours, so this is info and needs a day sustained; it stays open until the field is limed or acidified. Source: Wisconsin A2809, https://cropsandsoils.extension.wisc.edu/nutrient-application-guidelines-for-field-vegetable-and-fruit-crops-in-wisconsin-a2809/soil-ph-and-lime-requirement/
